description: UI quality metrics, UX quality dimensions and the separate design-system adherence verdict of the Forward unified product pipeline (forward spec/product-pipeline.md, 'UI quality: five mother metrics' and 'UX quality: equivalent journey measures'; spec/design-system-lifecycle.md, 'Separate adherence verdict'), with the DSX rules, measures and tools that feed each one. Source of the quality sections of tools/ux-lint/audit.mjs and of tools/ux-lint/criteria.mjs. Principle ids are the Forward catalog (heuristic_principles in forward spec/dimensions/quality-attributes.toml); DSX rules are probes that cite them, never a parallel catalog.
aggregation: none: every metric, dimension and criterion gets its own verdict; there is no score or weighted average, and a raw rule count is a diagnostic, never a verdict

verdicts.pass: a declared criterion was measured against its target with admissible evidence and met it
verdicts.fail: a declared criterion was measured and missed its target, or a blocking finding is open against it
verdicts.unknown: no criterion, no baseline where the target needs one, no measurement, or only synthetic evidence; never silently pass
verdicts.not-applicable: declared not applicable with a reason (for example a backend-only objective)

evidence_classes.observed: measured on the artifact itself: a probe, detector or script run on captures, geometry, the flow map or a browser journey
evidence_classes.expert-inferred: a reviewer's judgment citing a named principle (I8); labeled as inference, not measurement
evidence_classes.human: observed behaviour of real participants or production telemetry within privacy bounds
evidence_classes.synthetic: simulated users, agent runs or generated data; generates hypotheses, never passes a criterion (Forward fde-design 'User validation', USE-14)

verification_modes.automatic: a DSX detector or measure answers most of the question from captures, geometry or the flow map
verification_modes.mixed: automatic probes answer part; the rest needs expert judgment against the cited principles
verification_modes.judgment: expert review against named principles; automatic signals are diagnostics only
verification_modes.human: only observed people (or production telemetry) can answer it; agent completion is not evidence (USE-14)

words.detail: visible words of the surface capture (tools/ux-lint/variations.mjs measureCapture: content without header/nav, dialog only when one is open)

primary-actions.detail: visible primary actions on the surface capture (UX.md selectors.primary)

dialog-open.detail: 1 when the surface capture shows an open dialog

journey-steps.detail: transitions of the declared journey in .dsx/maps/flows-<module>.json

open-findings.detail: open findings of the rules named after the colon (open-findings:T1,L1) on the surface, or of the metric's DSX rules when no rule is named

ui_metrics.name: Information density
ui_metrics.operational_measure: Relevant information per visible area; scan/task time at realistic volume; overflow and zoom behaviour.
ui_metrics.gate_question: Can the intended user find needed information within the declared bound without losing readability?
evidence: screenshots at realistic volume (20+ rows, long names)
ui_metrics.caveat: More density is not automatically better: the register decides.
ui_metrics.automatic: words per surface, line length (L7), alignment (L4), archetype regions present (L9)
ui_metrics.judgment: relevance of what is shown for the job; density against the register; realistic volume
ui_metrics.human: scan/task time when the bound is a time

ui_metrics.name: Semantic economy
ui_metrics.operational_measure: Duplicate labels/concepts, unexplained terms, competing synonyms, text needed to identify an object or action.
ui_metrics.gate_question: Is each term necessary, consistent with the glossary and comprehensible?
ui_metrics.automatic: implementation terms, forbidden terms, synonyms between screens, generated-text marks
ui_metrics.judgment: whether a term is necessary and comprehensible to the persona

ui_metrics.name: Action topology
ui_metrics.operational_measure: Primary actions per task, distance and order from context to action, navigation depth and recovery reachability.
ui_metrics.gate_question: Are actions located at the correct object/cardinality and decision point, with one primary action per screen?
ui_metrics.automatic: primary actions per region, declared position, destructive labels, exits and back paths
ui_metrics.human: none required unless the criterion is discoverability

ui_metrics.name: Visual hierarchy alignment
ui_metrics.operational_measure: Order, emphasis and grouping of job-critical information versus the intended reading/decision sequence.
ui_metrics.gate_question: Does prominence match task priority and domain grouping across states?
dsx_measures: geometry: visual weight in the first fold, heading scale, proximity (tools/ux-lint/measure.mjs)
ui_metrics.automatic: single h1, heading scale, competing emphasis, proximity, primary above the fold
ui_metrics.judgment: whether the emphasized element is the job-critical one in each state
ui_metrics.human: none required unless the criterion is a reading sequence

ui_metrics.name: Interaction friction
ui_metrics.operational_measure: Unnecessary steps, repeated input, context switches, errors, recovery effort and latency.
ui_metrics.gate_question: Does the task stay within its declared effort and response bounds, including failure and resume?
ui_metrics.automatic: journey length, dialogs per step, labelled fields, error exits
ui_metrics.human: latency and time on task need a running build or telemetry

ux_dimensions.name: Task effectiveness
ux_dimensions.baseline_measure: Completion and correct domain outcome per actor/scenario, including error and resume.
ux_dimensions.gate_question: Does each actor reach the correct domain outcome in each declared scenario, error and resume included?
evidence: observed human completion when validating discoverability
ux_dimensions.automatic: dead ends and broken transitions in the map; missing error exits
ux_dimensions.judgment: whether the domain outcome is the correct one (DOM-3)
ux_dimensions.human: completion by unprepared people; an agent completing the journey only proves the path exists

ux_dimensions.name: Cognitive economy
ux_dimensions.baseline_measure: Decisions, terminology interpretations, recall burden, comprehension failures.
ux_dimensions.gate_question: Does the journey ask for no more decisions, interpretations and recall than the intended model declares?
evidence: human observations or a cited heuristic, labeled
ux_dimensions.judgment: decisions and recall burden against the intended model

ux_dimensions.name: Journey topology
ux_dimensions.baseline_measure: Steps, handoffs, dead ends, responsibility and recovery paths.
ux_dimensions.gate_question: Does every journey have valid exits, a recovery path and, at each handoff, recipient context, notification and deadline?
evidence: recipient context, notification/deadline and valid exits
ux_dimensions.automatic: exits, back paths, journey length, stacked dialogs, screens outside journeys, blueprint orphans

ux_dimensions.name: Expectation/feedback alignment
ux_dimensions.baseline_measure: Predicted versus actual state/result; feedback visibility and time.
ux_dimensions.gate_question: Does every action show its result and state change within the declared time, as the intended model predicts?
ux_dimensions.automatic: required states captured, error guidance, exits from empty/error

ux_dimensions.name: Effort and recovery
ux_dimensions.baseline_measure: Time on task, repeated entry, error frequency, abandonment and recovery cost.
ux_dimensions.gate_question: Do time, repeated entry, errors and recovery cost stay within the declared bounds, by keyboard too?
ux_dimensions.automatic: labelled fields, destructive labels, error guidance, target size
ux_dimensions.judgment: recovery cost of each error path

ds_adherence.rule: Design-system adherence has its own verdict per changed consumer (pass/fail/unknown/not-applicable, with foundation revision, scope and evidence). Passing adherence cannot compensate for a poor task topology; passing UI quality cannot excuse unexplained DS drift.

checks.name: Tokens and kit
checks.evidence: consumer/source diff, raw-value and duplicate search with documented exceptions

checks.name: Semantics
checks.evidence: glossary, status/action meaning, object/cardinality, allowed composition

checks.name: Rendered parity
checks.evidence: approved reference/wireframe comparison across affected states, themes and viewports

checks.name: Interaction and accessibility
checks.evidence: keyboard/focus/zoom, APG contract, axe, recovery/race probes

checks.name: Adoption
checks.evidence: consumer list, migrations/deprecations, rollback and explicit debt against the declared revision scope

heuristics.note: supporting knowledge: Nielsen heuristics justify findings that cite USE principles

cognitive-laws.note: supporting knowledge: UX laws size findings, they do not decide verdicts
